Call a single tool on an environment's MCP edge and print its result.

The bearer token is minted for this call from the desktop identity and never handled by the caller, so a script or agent driving an environment cannot be stopped by an expired token. The call goes to the environment's local MCP port, which requires the port-forward `erun open` establishes.

A tool can change the environment: whatever the named tool does, this runs it.

Usage:
  erun mcp call [flags]

Examples:
  erun mcp call --tool version
  erun mcp call --tenant acme --environment dev --tool raw --args '{"command":["git","status"]}'
  erun mcp call --tool list --output json

Flags:
      --args string          Tool arguments as a JSON object (default: no arguments)
      --dry-run              Resolve and trace mutating actions without executing them.
      --environment string   Target a specific environment; requires --tenant
  -h, --help                 help for call
      --tenant string        Target a specific tenant (default: the current scope)
      --tool string          Name of the tool to call, as listed by 'erun mcp tools'

Global Flags:
      --output string   Result format: text (default, human stream) or json (structured result on stdout for orchestrators). (default "text")
      --time            Print the elapsed runtime after the command finishes.
  -v, --verbose count   Increase verbosity: -v streams external tool output, -vv adds erun command traces.
